newsitem.title: USA: US Senator calls for cash machine surcharge study.
newsitem.headline: US Senator calls for cash machine surcharge study.

text.p: Senate Banking Committee chairman Alfonse D'Amato called Wednesday for a study of surcharges imposed on transactions at automatic teller machines.

"ATM operators are slapping the American consumer with double ATM surcharges for each transaction," D'Amato said. "Technological advances are supposed to lower costs and increase convenience, not serve as vehicles to gouge consumers."
Since April, some banks have begun charging a fee for use of their ATMs by customers of other banks.

The New York Republican, a frequent critic of the surcharges, asked the General Accounting Office to survey the situation and determine the average surcharge and the percentage of banks imposing such charges, among other issues.

Until last year, the major electronic payment networks prohibited ATM operators from charging fees to customers of other institutions. But the ban was lifted as of April and consumers can now be charged twice when they use a teller machine from a bank other than their own.
D'Amato introduced legislation in the last Congress to ban the practice.
Senate Banking Committee will closely examine the surcharges next year, D'Amato said.

"Financial service providers must understand that Congress will not permit them to use ATMs and other new technologies to exploit consumers with exorbitant fees and anti-competitive practices," the Senator said.
The American Bankers Association has defended surcharges, arguing that the fees give ATM operators an incentive to install more machines and provide consumers with greater choice.
